mainTopic: The end of the צריכותא about where the fire for the קטורת is taken from, and רבי מאיר's ruling (via בר קפרא) that leftover limbs of a עולה get their own מערכה, even on שבת. The ruling is explained as referring to פסולין, but only when the fire has already caught them.
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier צריכותא: both 'מעל המזבח' and 'מלפני ה'' are needed, so fire for the קטורת may be taken even from the sides of the מזבח. Then רבי אלעזר quotes בר קפרא: רבי מאיר said that leftover limbs of a עולה get their own מערכה, even on שבת. The גמרא asks what this adds to the משנה's four מערכות. רבי אבין answers that it teaches the rule even for פסולין. The גמרא then limits this to limbs that the fire has already caught, and gives a second version that applies this limit to valid limbs as well. Next the גמרא asks why 'even on שבת' was needed, since the משנה already has five מערכות on יום הכפורים. רב אחא בר יעקב gives an answer, but רבא rejects it because the משנה says 'every day', and the difficulty stays as a קשיא. The גמרא notes that this view disagrees with רב הונא, who holds that the end of the תמיד service does not override. רב חסדא and רבה disagree about what רב הונא meant: שבת or טומאה. אביי challenges both of them from the word 'במועדו'. רבה begins his defense with 'סופו כתחילתו', and his reply continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Both phrases are needed so fire can be taken from the sides too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its צריכותא. If only one phrase were written, we would think fire may not be taken from the side areas of the מזבח, so both phrases are necessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: But from this side or from that side, I would say no. Therefore it is necessary to write both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up an earlier argument. It explains why the פסוק needed two separate phrases to teach where the fire for the קטורת comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only one phrase, we would limit the place to the spot directly facing the היכל. The sides of the מזבח, which are not directly 'לפני ה'', would be excluded. Writing both phrases teaches that those side areas are valid too, so each phrase is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: side
I would say (a mistaken assumption)
it is necessary (to have both teachings)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of a discussion that started on the previous amud. It is not a new topic, so do not look for a question here. It is the final answer of a צריכותא, which explains why the תורה needed two phrases.

phrases.english: but from this side
phrases.notes: He means the sides of the מזבח that don't face the entrance of the היכל directly.

phrases.english: or from that side, I would say no,
therefore it is necessary (to write both).
phrases.notes: The standard closing word of a צריכותא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל מֵהַאי גִּיסָא וּמֵהַאי גִּיסָא אֵימָא לָא, צְרִיכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the צריכותא begun on the previous amud about the two phrases in the פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both 'מעל המזבח' and 'מלפני ה'' are needed, so fire for the קטורת may be taken even from the sides of the מזבח.

steps.title: Leftover limbs of a burnt-offering get their own arrangement, even on Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר quotes בר קפרא, who reports that רבי מאיר ruled: limbs of a עולה left unburned get a separate מערכה, and are arranged on it even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of בר קפרא: רבי מאיר used to say: limbs of a עולה that were left over, one makes a separate arrangement of wood for them and arranges them on it, even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רבי מאיר rules that leftover limbs of a עולה get their own pile of wood on the מזבח, and this is done even on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes limbs of a עולה from the night before were not fully burned. רבי מאיר says they are not just mixed into the main fire. Instead a separate מערכה is built for them. Adding 'even on שבת' shows that this arrangement counts as part of the עבודה, so it is allowed on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: limbs of a burnt-offering
that were left over (not fully burned)
a separate arrangement of wood on the מזבח
and he arranges them

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said in the name of bar Kappara:
Rabbi Meir would say:
limbs of a burnt-offering that were left over,
phrases.notes: Limbs left on the מזבח from the previous night that were not fully consumed.

phrases.english: one makes a separate arrangement for them
and arranges them, and even on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא, אוֹמֵר הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, related to the number of מערכות on the מזבח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leftover limbs of a עולה get a separate מערכה, and this is done even on שבת.

steps.title: Why teach this when the משנה already lists four arrangements?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what בר קפרא's report adds, since the משנה already quotes רבי מאיר as saying there were four מערכות every day. The fourth was for unburned limbs.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? We already learned in the משנה: every day there were four arrangements there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the teaching. It says the point seems repetitive, because the משנה already said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier משנה, רבי מאיר counts four מערכות every day. The fourth is for limbs and fats that were not burned the night before. So a separate arrangement for leftover limbs is already known. Why does בר קפרא need to repeat it?

keyTerms.meaning: what is he teaching us? (what is new here?)
four wood arrangements on the מזבח

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
We already learned: on every day
phrases.notes: Quoting רבי מאיר's view in the earlier משנה (יומא מה.).

phrases.english: there were four arrangements there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 2 as repeating what the משנה already says.
steps.kashyaTarget: בר קפרא's report of רבי מאיר's ruling about a separate מערכה for leftover limbs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already quotes רבי מאיר as having four מערכות, including one for unburned limbs. So the new teaching seems to add nothing.

steps.title: The teaching is about limbs of disqualified offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין answers that בר קפרא's teaching is needed only for limbs of פסולין, disqualified offerings. Even those get the separate מערכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין said: it was needed only for disqualified offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבין answers the challenge. He shows that בר קפרא is teaching something new that the משנה did not cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה was talking about limbs of valid offerings. Some פסולין, if already brought up on the מזבח, are not taken down. בר קפרא teaches that even these disqualified limbs get their own מערכה, even on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: it was needed only for
disqualified offerings

phrases.english: Rabbi Avin said:
It was needed only for disqualified offerings.
phrases.notes: He means disqualified offerings that, once they're already up on the מזבח, aren't taken back down (אם עלו לא ירדו).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לִפְסוּלִין
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the teaching refers to a different situation than the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think only valid limbs get a separate מערכה, and disqualified ones do not deserve that treatment, certainly not on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even limbs of פסולין that stay on the מזבח get their own מערכה, even on שבת.

steps.title: Only when the fire has already caught them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits רבי אבין's answer. The separate מערכה for disqualified limbs applies only if the fire already took hold of them. If not, no.
steps.simpleTranslation: And specifically when the fire has taken hold of them. But if the fire has not taken hold of them, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to the rule it just explained. Disqualified limbs get a separate arrangement only if they have already started burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the fire has caught disqualified limbs, they belong to the מזבח and are not removed. So we make sure they finish burning. If the fire never caught them, they are taken down instead, so no special מערכה is built for them.

keyTerms.meaning: and specifically / only
the fire took hold of them (they began to burn)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר (via בר קפרא): leftover limbs get their own מערכה, even on שבת. This adds to the משנה because it covers פסולין, but only those the fire has already caught.
steps.whyThisMatters: This connects the separate-מערכה rule to the general law about פסולין on the מזבח. Whether the fire has taken hold decides if they stay up and are burned or are taken down.

phrases.english: And specifically when the fire has taken hold of them,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא מָשְׁלָה בָּהֶן הָאוּר — לֹא.
phrases.english: but if the fire has not taken hold of them, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי אבין's answer in step 4 to a specific case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Disqualified limbs get a separate מערכה only if the fire already took hold of them. Otherwise they are not burned this way.

steps.title: A second version: valid or disqualified, only if the fire took hold
steps.stepSummary: A second version of the limit says the separate מערכה is made for limbs of both valid and disqualified offerings, but only if the fire already took hold of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say a different version: for both valid offerings and disqualified offerings, if the fire already took hold of the limbs, yes, they get a separate מערכה. If not, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the limit from Step 5. In this version, the 'fire took hold' condition applies to all limbs, valid and disqualified alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, only disqualified limbs needed the fire to have taken hold. In this version, even valid limbs get the separate מערכה only if they already started burning. So the condition no longer depends on whether the offering is valid or disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: Valid offerings
Disqualified offerings
The fire has taken hold of them

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In the first version (Step 5), the 'fire took hold' condition applies only to disqualified limbs. In this second version, it applies to valid limbs too.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Both valid offerings and disqualified offerings,
if the fire has taken hold of them, yes,
and if not, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative version of the limit stated in Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The separate מערכה applies to valid and disqualified limbs alike, but only when the fire has already taken hold of them.

steps.title: Why say 'even on שבת' when the משנה already teaches it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what בר קפרא's words 'even on שבת' add. The משנה already says there are five מערכות on יום הכפורים, a day when work is forbidden just like on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for 'even on שבת': we already learned this in the משנה, which says, 'and today there are five!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the last part of בר קפרא's report, 'even on שבת', and asks why it was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that on יום הכפורים there are five מערכות, so the extra מערכה for leftover limbs is made even then. Work is forbidden on יום הכפורים just as on שבת. So we already know the extra מערכה is made even on a day when work is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: And today (יום הכפורים) there are five מערכות
And even on שבת

phrases.english: And 'even on Shabbat':
phrases.notes: Quoting the end of בר קפרא's report.

phrases.english: We already learned: 'and today there are five!'
phrases.notes: On יום הכפורים, when work is forbidden like on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After dealing with the main part of בר קפרא's report (Steps 3-6), the גמרא now challenges its final clause.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'even on שבת' in בר קפרא's report.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy: the משנה's five מערכות on יום הכפורים already show the extra מערכה is made even when work is forbidden.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב: we might have limited it to יום הכפורים right after שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says בר קפרא's teaching is needed. From the משנה alone, we might think the fifth מערכה applies only when יום הכפורים falls on Sunday, because leftover fats from שבת are burned on יום הכפורים. On a midweek יום הכפורים, we might think there is no extra מערכה. בר קפרא teaches that there is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: It is needed. You might have thought this applies only when יום הכפורים falls right after שבת, since the fats of שבת offerings are burned on יום הכפורים. But in the middle of the week, no. So it teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב defends בר קפרא. The משנה alone could be read narrowly, and בר קפרא's teaching rules out that narrow reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's case of five מערכות on יום הכפורים could be explained by a special situation: יום הכפורים on Sunday, when leftover fats from שבת are burned. So one might think the extra מערכה exists only in that situation. בר קפרא shows that the extra מערכה is made always, even on a day when work is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary to teach this
You might have thought
Fats of שבת offerings left over to be burned
In the middle of the week
It teaches us (otherwise)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'שַׁבָּת' in 'בְּאֶמְצַע שַׁבָּת' means 'the week', not the day of שבת.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: אִיצְטְרִיךְ,
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said: It is necessary,
for you might have thought that this applies

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכָא דְּחָל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: only when Yom Kippur falls right after Shabbat,
since the fats of Shabbat offerings are burned on Yom Kippur,
but in the middle of the week, no;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: אִיצְטְרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy challenge of Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: the משנה alone could be read narrowly.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra מערכה on יום הכפורים exists only when it falls right after שבת, because of leftover שבת fats.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra מערכה is made always, even on a midweek יום הכפורים or on שבת.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה already says 'every day'
steps.stepSummary: רבא sharply rejects רב אחא בר יעקב's answer. The משנה already says there are four מערכות 'every day', so the rule clearly applies on all days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Who is this who does not care about his flour? We learned in the משנה: 'every day'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב אחא בר יעקב's answer, saying it was not carefully thought out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's words 'every day' already include every day of the week, with no special conditions. So the narrow reading that רב אחא suggested was never possible. That means בר קפרא's words 'even on שבת' still seem to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: Does not care about his flour: speaks without care, like someone careless with what he grinds
Every day: the משנה's wording about the four מערכות

phrases.english: Rava said:
Who is this who does not care about his flour?
phrases.notes: An expression for speaking without care.

phrases.english: Surely we learned 'every day'!

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב אחא בר יעקב's reason for why בר קפרא's teaching is needed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's words 'every day' already rule out limiting the extra מערכה to a יום הכפורים that falls after שבת.

steps.title: The difficulty stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes with קשיא: רבא's objection is not answered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer to רבא's objection and closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קשיא means the problem stays open. בר קפרא's words 'even on שבת' remain hard to explain, since the משנה already seems to teach that the extra מערכה is made on every day. The basic rule itself is not rejected. Only the reason for בר קפרא's extra words is left unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult: the objection stands without an answer

steps.whatToRemember: The separate מערכה for leftover limbs is made every day, even on שבת and יום הכפורים. The open question is only why בר קפרא needed to say 'even on שבת'. רב אחא בר יעקב's answer was rejected by רבא, and the גמרא leaves it as קשיא.
steps.confusionAlert: קשיא does not cancel the law. It only means that the reason given for בר קפרא's extra words did not hold up.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רבא's rejection in Step 9 as unanswered.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The redundancy of 'even on שבת' in בר קפרא's report remains an unresolved difficulty.

steps.title: This view conflicts with רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the opinion that an extra מערכה is set up even on שבת disagrees with רב הונא. He holds that the beginning of the תמיד service overrides, but its end does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with רב הונא, who said: its beginning overrides, its end does not override.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the opinion just discussed (an extra מערכה even on שבת) clashes with a ruling of רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an extra מערכה is set up on שבת to burn limbs, then the final stage of the offering (burning the limbs) overrides שבת. רב הונא holds that only the beginning of the service (slaughtering, sprinkling the blood) overrides, while the end does not. So the two views cannot both be right.

keyTerms.meaning: It disagrees with
Its beginning, the early stages of the service such as slaughtering and sprinkling the blood
Its end, the final stage such as burning the limbs and fats on the מזבח
Overrides or pushes aside a prohibition

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rav Huna,
who said: its beginning overrides,
phrases.notes: The early stages of the offering's service.

phrases.english: its end does not override.
phrases.notes: The final stage, burning the parts on the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the opinion that the extra מערכה is set up even on שבת, and shows that it conflicts with another אמורא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: the beginning of the service overrides, the end does not. This contradicts setting up a מערכה on שבת for burning limbs.

steps.title: Restating רב הונא's rule for closer study
steps.stepSummary: With 'גופא', the גמרא quotes רב הונא's statement in full so it can analyze it on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Returning to the matter itself: רב הונא said: the תמיד, its beginning overrides, its end does not override.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new discussion. It restates רב הונא's rule so it can examine what he really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'גופא' signals that the גמרא is moving away from the earlier topic to study a quoted statement directly. Here we learn the rule is about the תמיד, the daily offering. The phrase 'does not override' does not say which prohibition is meant. The next step asks this, and Steps 14-15 answer it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': the גמרא returns to study a quoted statement directly
The daily communal offering, brought every morning and afternoon

phrases.english: Returning to the matter itself.
Rav Huna said:
The daily offering: its beginning overrides,
its end does not override.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the statement quoted in Step 11 and opens a separate analysis of it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The beginning of the תמיד service overrides a prohibition, but its end does not.

steps.title: What does 'does not override' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which prohibition the end of the תמיד service fails to override.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רב הונא's words. This sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא did not say which prohibition he meant. It could be שבת, or it could be the rule against bringing an offering in a state of טומאה. The question opens that point.

keyTerms.meaning: What? Used to ask for clarification

steps.confusionAlert: Until now we assumed רב הונא was talking about שבת. This question shows that this is not obvious. He might be talking about טומאה instead.

phrases.english: What is meant by 'does not override'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the unclear phrase in the rule restated in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which prohibition the end of the תמיד service does not override: שבת or טומאה.

steps.title: רב חסדא: it overrides שבת but not טומאה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the end of the service overrides שבת but does not override טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: it overrides שבת, but it does not override טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives the first answer. The end of the תמיד may be done on שבת, but it may not be done in a state of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב חסדא, רב הונא was not talking about שבת at all. Both the beginning and the end override שבת. The difference is only about טומאה: the beginning may be done in טומאה if needed, but the end may not.

keyTerms.meaning: Overrides שבת, so the service may be done even though it involves forbidden work
Ritual impurity. Normally offerings may not be brought in this state

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
It overrides Shabbat,
but it does not override ritual impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The end of the service overrides שבת but not טומאה.

steps.title: רבה: it overrides טומאה but not שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבה (the printed text has 'רבא' in parentheses, but the accepted reading is רבה) gives the opposite explanation: the end of the service overrides טומאה but not שבת. This is not the same רבא who spoke in Step 9.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה said: it overrides טומאה, but it does not override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives the reverse answer. The end of the תמיד may be done in טומאה, but not on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reading matches how the גמרא first understood רב הונא in Step 11: the end of the service does not override שבת. So the last stage, burning the limbs, waits until after שבת, while טומאה does not hold it back.

keyTerms.meaning: The printed text has (רבא) in parentheses, marking it as a deleted reading. The correct reading is רבה, the teacher of אביי, who is not the רבא of Step 9.

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא and רבה say exact opposites. Keep a simple chart: רב חסדא = yes שבת, no טומאה. רבה = yes טומאה, no שבת. Do not confuse רבה with רבא from Step 9, who holds the extra מערכה is made even on שבת.

phrases.english: And Rabba said:
It overrides ritual impurity,
but it does not override Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the opposite answer to the same question that רב חסדא answered in Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The end of the service overrides טומאה but not שבת.

steps.title: אביי's challenge: the word 'במועדו' covers שבת too
steps.stepSummary: אביי says both views are difficult. He begins with רבה: the word 'במועדו' teaches that the תמיד overrides טומאה, so it should equally teach that it overrides שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבה: Your view is difficult, and רב חסדא's view is difficult. Yours is difficult: why is טומאה different? Because it says 'במועדו', meaning even in טומאה. But for שבת too it says 'במועדו', meaning even on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי announces that he has a challenge against both opinions. He then starts with the challenge against רבה. The challenge against רב חסדא comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה says the end of the service overrides טומאה because the תורה says the תמיד must be brought 'במועדו', meaning at its set time no matter what. אביי argues that this same word also covers שבת. So רבה cannot use it for טומאה while denying that the end overrides שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: According to you, against your view
A difficulty or challenge
What is different? Asks why two cases are treated differently
'In its set time' (במדבר כח:ב). Teaches that the offering must be brought at its time under all conditions
Also, too

steps.whyThisMatters: 'במועדו' is the classic source that time-bound communal offerings override שבת and טומאה. אביי's point is that you cannot split the word: it applies to both.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him (to Rabba):
It is difficult for you, and it is difficult for Rav Chisda.
phrases.notes: An opening that announces two separate challenges.

phrases.english: It is difficult for you:
What is different about ritual impurity?
Because it is written 'in its season', meaning even in impurity.
Shabbat too: 'in its season', meaning even on Shabbat!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרָבָא: לְדִידָךְ קַשְׁיָא, וּלְרַב חִסְדָּא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation in Step 15 and announces a coming attack on the one in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view that the end of the תמיד overrides טומאה but not שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same verse, 'במועדו', is the source for overriding both טומאה and שבת. Using it for one and not the other is inconsistent.

steps.title: אביי challenges רב חסדא using the same verse
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that רב חסדא has no reason to treat שבת differently from טומאה, since the same word 'במועדו' covers both.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is difficult for רב חסדא: Why is שבת different? Because it is written 'במועדו', which means even on שבת. Then for טומאה too, 'במועדו' should mean even in טומאה!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of אביי's challenge. He now turns against רב חסדא, just as he turned against רבה in the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said the end of the service overrides שבת but not טומאה. אביי points out that 'במועדו' is the source for both rules, so it should work the same way for both. If the word is strong enough to override שבת, it should also override טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: And for רב חסדא it is difficult
What is the difference? Why treat this one differently?
Also, too
Even

phrases.english: And for Rav Chisda it is difficult:
What is different about Shabbat,
phrases.notes: Why does the end of the service override Shabbat in his view?

phrases.english: because it is written 'in its season', meaning even on Shabbat,
then impurity too: 'in its season',
meaning even in impurity!
phrases.notes: The same verse should work for both cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This mirrors step 16. There אביי attacked רבה, and here he attacks רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's view that the end of the service overrides שבת but not טומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both rules come from the single word 'במועדו'. The verse does not make any distinction between them, so treating שבת and טומאה differently has no basis.

steps.title: רבה declares that neither view is difficult
steps.stepSummary: רבה responds to אביי that the challenge works against neither his own view nor רב חסדא's.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is not difficult for me, and it is not difficult for רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה opens his defense with a general claim. This line sets up the next moves, where he will explain each view one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי claimed that 'במועדו' forces the same rule for שבת and טומאה. רבה says each view can explain why the two prohibitions are treated differently. He promises two separate explanations.

keyTerms.meaning: For me, according to my view
It is not difficult

phrases.english: He said to him:
It is not difficult for me,
and it is not difficult for Rav Chisda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא לְדִידִי קַשְׁיָא, וְלָא לְרַב חִסְדָּא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This responds to אביי's double challenge in steps 16 and 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Announcement of separate defenses for both views
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'במועדו' must apply the same way to שבת and טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each view has its own reason for treating the two differently. These reasons will be explained next.

steps.title: רבה's defense: the end of the service is like its beginning
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains his own view. He says the end of the service follows the same rule as its beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: For me it is not difficult: its end is like its beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה begins with his own view. He gives the principle 'סופו כתחילתו' to explain why the end of the service overrides טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main תמיד service overrides טומאה because of 'במועדו'. רבה says the end of the service is simply treated like that beginning, so it overrides טומאה too. With this principle, he no longer needs to read 'במועדו' as applying to the end of the service by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Its end, meaning the final part of the service
Like its beginning
Its end follows the same rule as its beginning

steps.confusionAlert: 'סופו כתחילתו' is רבה's reason for why the end overrides טומאה. It is not yet his explanation of why the end does not override שבת. Do not assume this line settles the שבת question.

phrases.english: For me it is not difficult:
its end is like its beginning,
phrases.notes: The end of the offering's service follows the same rule as the start of the service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This carries out the first half of the promise made in step 18 by defending רבה's own view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A new principle that treats the end of the service like its beginning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Why the end overrides טומאה must depend on reading 'במועדו' directly about the end, so it should override שבת equally.
steps.terutzMaskana: The end overrides טומאה because it takes on the status of the beginning, which overrides טומאה.
